description.narrative:
Cyclone Ditwah, which hit Sri Lanka on 28 November 2025, resulted in the worst flooding the country had seen in decades along with catastrophic landslides, affecting 2 million people across the whole country. Final death toll was 670. Over 233,000 families had to move to temporary shelter centres, and there was huge infrastructural damage to housing, hospitals, schools and factories, farmlands, potable water supply and irrigation systems, and communication systems. Due to inundation and damage to agricultural land throughout the country, an entire season's harvest was impacted and in many areas lost entirely. Massive losses of livestock and damage to fisheries and aquaculture sectors have further impacted Sri Lanka's food security and the livelihoods of small-scale food producers. $4.1 billion in direct damage. High rainfall continued after the cyclone, causing further flooding in the east and in some newly-impacted areas including Panama. By second half of January the rain was still falling in some areas (with some still underwater) and land damage remained.
This project follows on from an intervention by CRS in three particularly marginalised communities supported under a Rapid Release grant in December, seeking to address futher immediate-term needs (food, health and shelter) and engaging advocacy through dialogue between the impacted communiies, the environmental and wild life authorities, government actors and estate management to promote vigilance and responsibility with regard to ecologically destructive practices which could give rise to further natural disasters.
